import itertools

# Category order is inferred from the "correct" examples in the prompt.
# Directly evidenced pairwise constraints:
#   opinion < shape    (good circular bird, #28)
#   shape   < size     (square large walking wrench, #177)
#   size    < color    (little white pen, #27)
#   color   < age      (silly aqua new vase, #167)
#   age     < purpose  (new snorkeling bottle, #3)
#   material < origin  (cardboard egyptian shirt, #1)
# The examples never fix where material/origin sit relative to the other
# categories, so every total order consistent with the evidence is enumerated.

CATEGORIES = ("opinion", "shape", "size", "color", "age",
              "material", "origin", "purpose")

EVIDENCE = [
    ("opinion", "shape", "good circular bird (#28)"),
    ("shape", "size", "square large walking wrench (#177)"),
    ("size", "color", "little white pen (#27)"),
    ("color", "age", "silly aqua new vase (#167)"),
    ("age", "purpose", "new snorkeling bottle (#3)"),
    ("material", "origin", "cardboard egyptian shirt (#1)"),
]

LEX = {}


def add(cat, words):
    for w in words:
        LEX[w] = cat


add("opinion", ["good", "ridiculous", "terrible", "nice", "awful", "silly",
                "obnoxious", "repulsive", "mysterious", "lovely", "wonderful"])
add("shape", ["circular", "square", "prismlike", "pyramidal", "spherical",
              "rectangular", "triangular"])
add("size", ["little", "large", "huge", "big", "tiny", "medium-size",
             "midsize", "small", "massive", "enormous"])
add("color", ["teal", "magenta", "black", "violet", "red", "cyan", "white",
              "yellow", "pink", "aqua"])
add("age", ["ancient", "archaic", "old-fashioned", "old", "new"])
add("material", ["plastic", "wool", "wood", "paper", "steel", "leather",
                 "glass", "cardboard", "fiberglass"])
add("origin", ["brazilian", "mexican", "thai", "turkish", "ethiopian",
               "nigerian", "egyptian", "iranian", "russian"])
add("purpose", ["snorkeling", "exercise", "walking", "whittling", "driving",
                "drinking", "eating", "typing", "smoking", "hiking"])

OPTIONS = {
    "A": "plastic little teal ancient snorkeling circular terrible pencil",
    "B": "good square large black archaic drinking box",
    "C": "ridiculous circular huge magenta ancient exercise brazilian wool sunglasses",
    "D": "circular tiny red old-fashioned walking wood mexican plate",
    "E": "medium-size violet archaic whittling paper turkish knife",
    "F": "thai steel medium-size cyan archaic driving chair",
    "G": "turkish big white old drinking prismlike nice banana",
    "H": "midsize yellow new eating turkish wool knife",
    "I": "plastic ethiopian big black archaic snorkeling box",
    "J": "nigerian leather small pink ancient typing spherical ridiculous saw",
}

# Enumerate every total order of the categories satisfying the evidence.
consistent = []
for perm in itertools.permutations(CATEGORIES):
    pos = {c: i for i, c in enumerate(perm)}
    if all(pos[a] < pos[b] for a, b, _ in EVIDENCE):
        consistent.append(pos)

total = len(consistent)
print("evidence constraints:", len(EVIDENCE))
print("consistent category orders:", total)

# Map each option's adjectives to categories; the last token is the noun.
option_cats = {}
for key, sentence in OPTIONS.items():
    adjs = sentence.split()[:-1]
    unmapped = [w for w in adjs if w not in LEX]
    if unmapped:
        raise SystemExit(f"UNMAPPED words in option {key}: {unmapped}")
    option_cats[key] = [LEX[w] for w in adjs]

always, never, sometimes = [], [], []
for key, cats in option_cats.items():
    ok_count = 0
    for pos in consistent:
        if all(pos[cats[i]] < pos[cats[i + 1]] for i in range(len(cats) - 1)):
            ok_count += 1
    seq = " > ".join(cats)
    print(f"{key}: order [{seq}] correct in {ok_count}/{total} orders")
    if ok_count == total:
        always.append(key)
    elif ok_count == 0:
        never.append(key)
    else:
        sometimes.append(key)

print("correct in every consistent order:", "".join(always) or "none")
print("correct in no consistent order:", "".join(never) or "none")
print("depends on unevidenced placement:", "".join(sometimes) or "none")

# Submitted answer is K (none correct). Test it directly.
if always:
    print("K: CHECK FAIL (option(s) " + "".join(always) +
          " are correct under every consistent order)")
else:
    print("K: CHECK PASS")

for key in sometimes:
    print(f"{key}: UNSUPPORTED (ordering of material/origin not fixed by examples)")
